components.note: 亻 (person) — 位 relates to a person's location.
立 (to stand) — the spot where a person stands gave 位 its meaning 'position' or 'place,' and later, a polite measure word for people.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 请帮我占一个位子,谢谢。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ zhàn yī gè wèizi, xièxie.
example.english: Please save a seat for me, thanks.
example.fact: Airplane economy seats have actually shrunk over time: standard seat width has dropped from about 18.5 inches in the 1980s to as little as 16.5 inches today, even as average passenger body size increased over the same period. Airlines made the tradeoff to fit more rows into the same fuselage length.

meanings: not having learned to do sth

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'

example.hanzi: 别担心,我不会告诉别人的。
example.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, wǒ bùhuì gàosù biérén de.
example.english: Don't worry, I won't tell anyone.
example.fact: Research by psychologist Michael Slepian found that people think about the secrets they're keeping roughly once a day on average, and that it's the mental burden of concealment itself — not the topic of the secret — that makes carrying one feel exhausting.

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 下一位选手准备上场了。
example.pinyin: Xià yī wèi xuǎnshǒu zhǔnbèi shàngchǎng le.
example.english: The next contestant is getting ready to go on stage.
example.fact: Glossophobia, the fear of public speaking, affects a large majority of people to some degree, and it triggers the same fight-or-flight surge of adrenaline that the body uses when facing a physical threat — the nervous system doesn't distinguish a stage from a predator.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 投 relates to throwing something with the hand
殳 (shū) gives a loose sound connection to 投's reading tóu
阝 (hill) — 降 originally related to coming down a hill or slope
夅 (jiàng) gives the sound — an exact match with 降's reading jiàng

example.hanzi: 敌军最终选择了投降。
example.pinyin: Díjūn zuìzhōng xuǎnzéle tóuxiáng.
example.english: The enemy army ultimately chose to surrender.
example.fact: Japan's formal World War II surrender took place aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay on September 2, 1945. The signing ceremony that ended a six-year global war lasted only about 23 minutes.

components.note: 毛 (fur, hair) — 表 originally pictured a fur garment worn on the outside.
衣 (clothing) — an outer fur wrap gave 表 its meaning of 'outer' or 'surface,' and later, 'to express' (showing something on the surface).
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'

example.hanzi: 湖的表面在阳光下闪闪发光。
example.pinyin: Hú de biǎomiàn zài yángguāng xià shǎnshǎn fāguāng.
example.english: The surface of the lake sparkles in the sunlight.
example.fact: Water's surface tension is strong enough that insects like the water strider can walk across it without breaking through, spreading their weight over thousands of tiny water-repelling hairs on each leg.

components.note: 手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'

example.hanzi: 那支箭正好击中了目标的中心。
example.pinyin: Nà zhī jiàn zhènghǎo jīzhòngle mùbiāo de zhōngxīn.
example.english: That arrow hit right in the center of the target.
example.fact: In Olympic target archery, athletes shoot from 70 meters away at a target face whose center ring is only about 12 centimeters wide — meaning a fraction of a degree of aiming error is the difference between a perfect score and a total miss.

components.note: 又 replaced the more complex phonetic component 雚 (guān) when 欢 was simplified from the traditional 歡; it keeps only a loose echo of that original sound, now read huān.
欠 depicts a person with an open mouth, as if yawning or gasping — an image of an open, expressive face that connects to 欢's meaning of joy and delight.
口 (mouth) — 呼 describes an action of the mouth, such as calling out or breathing.
乎 (hū) gives the sound — an exact match with 呼.

example.hanzi: 球迷们为进球欢呼起来。
example.pinyin: Qiúmímen wèi jìnqiú huānhū qǐlái.
example.english: The fans cheered for the goal.
example.fact: The loudest crowd roar ever recorded at a sports stadium reached 142.2 decibels, set by Kansas City Chiefs fans in 2014 — louder than a jet engine at takeoff, and loud enough to risk hearing damage with prolonged exposure.

components.note: 丶 (a dot) — represents the burning flame atop a lamp.
王 here depicts the base and stand of an oil lamp, not its usual meaning 'king' — the one who tends the flame became linked to 'master, lord, main.'
广 depicts a simple roofed building or shelter.
巾 (cloth) — together with a grass-like element above it, suggests a woven straw or cloth mat inside the shelter, giving 席 its meaning 'mat, seat.'

example.hanzi: 他被选为公司的新任主席。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi xuǎn wéi gōngsī de xīnrèn zhǔxí.
example.english: He was elected the company's new chairperson.
example.fact: Separating the chairperson and CEO roles into two different people is now standard governance practice at more than half of S&P 500 companies, up from roughly a fifth of them two decades earlier, as boards sought clearer checks on executive power.

components.note: 冫 (water) — 准 originally referred to a carpenter's level using water to check flatness, extended to 'standard, accurate, level.'
隹 (zhuī) gives a sound hint — 准 is pronounced zhǔn, sharing the base sound though the vowel and tone differ somewhat.
石 (stone) — 确 originally meant firm and solid like stone, extending to 'true, accurate, indeed.'
角 (jiǎo) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from què.

example.hanzi: 这个天气预报相当准确。
example.pinyin: Zhège tiānqì yùbào xiāngdāng zhǔnquè.
example.english: This weather forecast is quite accurate.
example.fact: One-day weather forecasts are correct roughly 90% of the time, but accuracy drops sharply after about a week, because the atmosphere behaves as a chaotic system where tiny measurement errors roughly double every few days — the origin of the popular 'butterfly effect' idea.

components.note: 知 (to know) forms the upper part of the character.
日 (sun, clarity) — knowledge seen as clearly as the sun gave 智 its meaning 'wisdom.'
心 (mind) — 慧 describes a sharp, clear mind, 'intelligent, wise.'
彗 (huì) gives the sound — an exact match with 慧.

example.hanzi: 老人的智慧来自多年的生活经验。
example.pinyin: Lǎorén de zhìhuì láizì duōnián de shēnghuó jīngyàn.
example.english: The old man's wisdom comes from years of life experience.
example.fact: Aging research shows that while raw processing speed tends to decline with age, 'crystallized intelligence' — accumulated knowledge and judgment — keeps growing well into a person's sixties and seventies, which is part of why wisdom-related skills often peak later in life.

components.note: 火 (fire) — linked to ritual fires once used to try to communicate with spirits
彐 (jì) gives a sound distantly related to 灵's reading líng, having drifted apart considerably over time
咸 (all, together) — 感 relates to a shared reaction.
心 (heart) — feelings that stir the heart gave 感 its meaning 'to feel' or 'emotion.'

example.hanzi: 这幅画的灵感来自一次日出。
example.pinyin: Zhè fú huà de línggǎn láizì yī cì rìchū.
example.english: This painting's inspiration came from a sunrise.
example.fact: Sunrises look reddish-orange because sunlight passing through more atmosphere at a low angle scatters away shorter blue wavelengths, a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, leaving mostly the longer red and orange wavelengths to reach the eye.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 漫 describes water overflowing and spreading everywhere.
曼 (màn) gives the sound — an exact match with 漫.
画 depicts a picture set within a frame — the traditional form 畫 additionally showed a hand holding a brush above it.

example.hanzi: 他从小就喜欢看漫画。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xǐhuan kàn mànhuà.
example.english: He has loved reading comics since he was little.
example.fact: At its 1995 peak, the Japanese manga magazine Weekly Shonen Jump sold over 6 million copies per issue — more circulation in a single week than most countries' entire national magazine markets combined.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — 莎 originally named a type of sedge grass.
沙 (shā) gives the sound — an exact match with 莎.
扌 (hand) — relates directly to 拉's meaning 'to pull, drag,' an action done by hand.
立 (lì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted noticeably from lā.

example.hanzi: 莎拉每天早上都去跑步。
example.pinyin: Shālā měitiān zǎoshang dōu qù pǎobù.
example.english: Sarah goes jogging every morning.
example.fact: The long-running Copenhagen City Heart Study linked regular light-to-moderate jogging to several added years of life expectancy compared with being sedentary, with the biggest benefit found at just one to two and a half hours of jogging per week — more wasn't necessarily better.

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — 性 relates to inner nature or character.
生 (shēng) gives a hint of the sound — 性 is pronounced xìng, a related sound though the initial has shifted.
冖 (a roof/house) — the home being welcomed into.
友 (a friend) — brought close into one's home; the traditional form 愛 also includes 心 ('heart') in the middle — the source of 爱's meaning 'to love.'

example.hanzi: 这本书探讨了亲密关系中的性爱话题。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū tàntǎole qīnmì guānxì zhōng de xìng'ài huàtí.
example.english: This book explores the topic of intimacy in close relationships.
example.fact: The hormone oxytocin, often called the 'bonding hormone,' is released during both physical intimacy and childbirth, and studies have measured its role in promoting trust and social bonding between the people who experience its release together.

components.note: 饣 (food) — 饭 names cooked rice, a meal.
反 (fǎn) gives the sound — an exact match with 饭.
广 (shelter/building) — 店 names a building used for business.
占 (zhàn) gives a sound distantly related to diàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 我们在那家饭店预订了一张桌子。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài nà jiā fàndiàn yùdìngle yī zhāng zhuōzi.
example.english: We reserved a table at that restaurant.
example.fact: Sobrino de Botín in Madrid, which opened in 1725, holds the Guinness World Record for the oldest restaurant in continuous operation — it's even mentioned by name in Ernest Hemingway's novel The Sun Also Rises.

meanings: to do sth of one's own accord
opposite: passive 被動|被动[bei4 dong4]

components.note: 丶 (a dot) — represents the burning flame atop a lamp.
王 here depicts the base and stand of an oil lamp, not its usual meaning 'king' — the one who tends the flame became linked to 'master, lord, main.'
力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.

example.hanzi: 她主动帮同事解决了问题。
example.pinyin: Tā zhǔdòng bāng tóngshì jiějuéle wèntí.
example.english: She took the initiative to help her colleague solve the problem.
example.fact: Organizational psychology research consistently links proactive, initiative-taking behavior at work with faster promotions and higher job satisfaction, in part because acting before being asked signals competence to supervisors more clearly than simply completing assigned tasks.

components.note: 平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.
日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form

example.hanzi: 平时他六点就起床了。
example.pinyin: Píngshí tā liù diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
example.english: Ordinarily, he gets up at six o'clock.
example.fact: The human body's internal clock, run by a cluster of neurons called the suprachiasmatic nucleus, naturally cycles on a period of about 24.2 hours — slightly longer than a solar day — which is why daily exposure to light is needed to keep it in sync with the outside world.

components.note: 又 (hand) and 寸 (also derived from a hand shape) — together suggesting two hands matching or corresponding, related to 对's meaning 'correct, matching.'
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'

example.hanzi: 银行就在超市的对面。
example.pinyin: Yínháng jiù zài chāoshì de duìmiàn.
example.english: The bank is right across from the supermarket.
example.fact: The Italian city of Bologna has around 38 kilometers of covered porticoes lining the streets facing each other, a network so extensive and historically significant that UNESCO added it to the World Heritage List in 2021.

components.note: 囗 (an enclosure) surrounds the character.
人 (person) sits inside — a person trapped in an enclosure, giving 囚 its meaning 'prisoner, to confine.'
犭 (dog) — 犯 originally related to a dog attacking, later extended to any act of violation
㔾 (jié) gives a sound distantly related to 犯's reading fàn, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 那名囚犯已经服刑十年了。
example.pinyin: Nà míng qiúfàn yǐjīng fúxíng shí nián le.
example.english: That prisoner has already served ten years.
example.fact: Alcatraz federal prison operated for 29 years and, despite its reputation as escape-proof, recorded at least 14 separate escape attempts involving 36 inmates. Officially none succeeded, though the fate of three men from the famous 1962 escape was never conclusively determined.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 骗 originally described swinging up onto a horse, later extended figuratively to 'to trick, to swindle.'
扁 (biǎn) shares the rhyme -ian with piàn, and both use a bilabial initial (b/p) — only voicing and tone differ.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 他说的话都是骗人的。
example.pinyin: Tā shuō dehuà dōu shì piànrén de.
example.english: Everything he said was a lie.
example.fact: A large meta-analysis of deception research found that people can spot lies from behavior alone with only about 54% accuracy — barely better than a coin flip — because there is no single reliable physical 'tell' that reveals lying.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — 联 originally meant 'connected, linked,' perhaps through the image of joined loops.
关 (guān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lián.

合 pictures a lid (亼) fitting neatly down over an opening or container (口) below it — the image of two matching pieces closing together, which gave rise to the meanings 'to close' and 'to combine, unite.'

example.hanzi: 两家公司决定联合开发新产品。
example.pinyin: Liǎng jiā gōngsī juédìng liánhé kāifā xīn chǎnpǐn.
example.english: The two companies decided to jointly develop a new product.
example.fact: The United Nations was founded in 1945 by 51 countries and now counts 193 member states, making it the largest intergovernmental organization on Earth, even though most of its General Assembly resolutions are non-binding.

components.note: A drawing of a ridged, pointed animal horn.
艹 (grass/plant) — 落 relates to leaves or plants falling
洛 (luò) gives the sound — 落 is also pronounced luò, an exact match

example.hanzi: 猫躲在房间的角落里睡觉。
example.pinyin: Māo duǒ zài fángjiān de jiǎoluò lǐ shuìjiào.
example.english: The cat is hiding in the corner of the room, sleeping.
example.fact: A 2014 study on shelter cats found that cats given an enclosed hiding box adjusted to a new environment and showed lower stress-hormone levels faster than cats without one, supporting the idea that cats instinctively seek tight, corner-like spaces to feel secure.

components.note: 页 (head) — 预 relates to looking ahead or foreseeing beforehand
予 (yǔ) gives a sound close to 预's reading yù, differing mainly in tone
口 (mouth) — with strokes above depicting a tongue sticking out — the image of speaking, the source of 言's meaning 'speech, words, language.'

example.hanzi: 他的预言最后竟然成真了。
example.pinyin: Tā de yùyán zuìhòu jìngrán chéngzhēn le.
example.english: His prophecy actually came true in the end.
example.fact: Ancient Greeks traveled across the Mediterranean to consult the Oracle of Delphi, a priestess called the Pythia who delivered prophecies in a trance. Modern geological studies suggest fissures beneath the temple may have released ethylene gas, which could help explain her altered state.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
帀 (a banner or covering) — flying above the scene.
刂 (a knife) — wielded with skill beneath the banner, an image of expertise giving 师 its meaning 'master, teacher, expert.'

example.hanzi: 他是国际知名的围棋大师。
example.pinyin: Tā shì guójì zhīmíng de wéiqí dàshī.
example.english: He is an internationally renowned Go master.
example.fact: The board game Go has more possible board positions than there are atoms in the observable universe, an estimate as high as 10^170, which is a major reason computers struggled to master it until AlphaGo's breakthrough win in 2016.

components.note: 气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.
气 (air, gas) — atmosphere and mood are described using the word for air.
分 (fēn) gives the sound — an exact match for 氛.

example.hanzi: 派对上的气氛非常热烈。
example.pinyin: Pàiduì shàng de qìfēn fēicháng rèliè.
example.english: The atmosphere at the party was very lively.
example.fact: Earth's atmosphere has no sharp edge, but the internationally recognized boundary of space, the Kármán line, is set at 100 kilometers altitude — above which conventional aircraft can no longer generate enough lift, and vehicles must switch to rocket propulsion instead.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 批 relates to an action done by hand, such as marking or sorting
比 (bǐ) gives a loose sound connection to 批's reading pī
冫 (water) — 准 originally referred to a carpenter's level using water to check flatness, extended to 'standard, accurate, level.'
隹 (zhuī) gives a sound hint — 准 is pronounced zhǔn, sharing the base sound though the vowel and tone differ somewhat.

example.hanzi: 这项计划已经得到政府批准。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng jìhuà yǐjīng dédào zhèngfǔ pīzhǔn.
example.english: This plan has already received government approval.
example.fact: Getting a new drug approved in the United States takes on average more than a decade and costs upward of a billion dollars, largely because roughly 90% of drug candidates that enter clinical trials fail somewhere along the way and never reach approval.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — 脾 names a body organ, the spleen.
卑 (bēi) gives a sound close to pí, sharing a related initial though the rhyme has shifted.
气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.

example.hanzi: 他的脾气一向很好。
example.pinyin: Tā de píqi yīxiàng hěn hǎo.
example.english: He has always had a good temper.
example.fact: When a person becomes angry, the brain's amygdala can trigger a stress response in well under a second, releasing adrenaline before the slower, more rational prefrontal cortex has time to weigh in — part of why deliberately pausing before reacting actually gives the rational brain a chance to catch up.

components.note: 石 (rock) — 碎 describes something, often stone-like, broken into pieces.
卒 (zú) is only distantly related in sound to suì — the connection has drifted apart considerably over time.
A pictograph of half of a split tree trunk, shown in cross-section (compare 爿, the other half) — the source of 片's meaning 'a thin slice, piece.'

example.hanzi: 花瓶摔碎后留下了一地碎片。
example.pinyin: Huāpíng shuāisuì hòu liúxiàle yī dì suìpiàn.
example.english: After the vase shattered, fragments were left all over the floor.
example.fact: The European Space Agency estimates there are more than 130 million pieces of space debris smaller than a centimeter orbiting Earth, remnants of old satellites and rockets — even a paint fleck traveling at orbital speeds of roughly 28,000 km/h can damage a spacecraft.

components.note: 无's traditional form 無 originally pictured a dancer holding tasseled ornaments in each hand, a meaning later split off into the separate character 舞 ('to dance'). The character itself was borrowed purely for its sound to write the abstract negative 'without, nothing,' leaving no visual link to dancing.
罒 (a net) — the law closing in around wrongdoing
非 (wrong) — the wrongdoing itself, caught in the net

example.hanzi: 法院最终判他无罪。
example.pinyin: Fǎyuàn zuìzhōng pàn tā wúzuì.
example.english: The court ultimately found him not guilty.
example.fact: Since 1992, the Innocence Project has used DNA evidence to help exonerate more than 375 wrongfully convicted people in the United States, some of whom had already spent decades in prison, including time on death row.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 逃 means to escape or flee, involving movement.
兆 (zhào) gives a rhyme close to táo, with the initial shifted.
⺼ (flesh, body) — 脱 relates to taking something off the body.
兑 (duì) gives a sound close to tuō, sharing a related initial.

example.hanzi: 那只鸟趁机逃脱了笼子。
example.pinyin: Nà zhī niǎo chènjī táotuōle lóngzi.
example.english: That bird seized the chance to escape the cage.
example.fact: Octopuses are famous escape artists because they have no rigid skeleton and can squeeze through any opening larger than their beak, the one hard part of their body — a New Zealand octopus named Inky made international news in 2016 after sliding down a drainpipe back to the ocean.

components.note: 介 (jiè) gives a sound hint — 价 is pronounced jià, sharing the same initial consonant though the vowel has shifted.
木 (wood) — 格 originally meant a wooden branch or standard, extended to 'pattern, style, rule.'
各 (gè) gives a sound hint — 格 is pronounced gé, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这台电脑的价格比我想象的便宜。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái diànnǎo de jiàgé bǐ wǒ xiǎngxiàng de piányí.
example.english: This computer's price is cheaper than I imagined.
example.fact: Moore's Law, the 1965 observation that the number of transistors on a computer chip roughly doubles every two years, held remarkably true for decades and is a major reason computing power that once cost millions of dollars now fits in a phone costing a few hundred.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — ancient policy documents were written on bamboo strips
朿 (cì) gives a sound distantly related to 策's reading cè, having drifted apart over time
田 (field) — 略 originally related to surveying or dividing farmland
各 (gè) gives a sound distantly related to 略's reading lüè, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 教练在比赛中改变了策略。
example.pinyin: Jiàoliàn zài bǐsài zhōng gǎibiànle cèlüè.
example.english: The coach changed strategy during the match.
example.fact: In 1950, mathematician John Nash proved that any competitive game with a finite number of players and strategies has at least one stable outcome, now called a Nash equilibrium, where no player can benefit by changing strategy alone — the insight later won him a Nobel Prize in Economics.

components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 街角坐着一个老头在下棋。
example.pinyin: Jiējiǎo zuòzhe yī gè lǎotóu zài xiàqí.
example.english: An old man is sitting at the street corner playing chess.
example.fact: The longest officially recorded chess game lasted 269 moves and over 20 hours before ending in a draw, played between Ivan Nikolić and Goran Arsović in Belgrade in 1989 — arbiters eventually had to step in to bring it to a close.

components.note: 丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud
非 (two things back-to-back) — 靠 relates to leaning against or relying on something
告 (gào) gives a sound distantly related to 靠's reading kào, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 这台机器的性能非常可靠。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái jīqì de xìngnéng fēicháng kěkào.
example.english: This machine's performance is very reliable.
example.fact: The Voyager 1 spacecraft, launched in 1977 with computer technology far less powerful than a modern calculator, is still transmitting data from interstellar space more than 47 years later, a testament to conservative, redundant engineering built to far outlast its original mission.

components.note: 页 (head) — relates to 领's meaning 'neck, collar; to lead,' the head/neck area.
令 (lìng) gives a sound hint — 领 is pronounced lǐng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.
止 (a foot, stepping forward) — 先 pictures someone moving ahead of another.
儿 (a person) — one person stepping ahead of another gave 先 its meaning 'before' or 'first.'

example.hanzi: 我们的团队目前在比赛中领先。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen de tuánduì mùqián zài bǐsài zhōng lǐngxiān.
example.english: Our team is currently leading in the competition.
example.fact: Usain Bolt's 100-meter world record of 9.58 seconds, set in 2009, works out to an average speed of over 37 km/h, with radar tracking showing his peak speed during the race topping 44 km/h — faster than many neighborhood speed limits.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match
夂 (to go) — heading out.
田 (farm field) — going out to the fields ahead of the harvest season, the act of preparation giving 备 its meaning 'to prepare, get ready.'

example.hanzi: 登山队检查了所有装备才出发。
example.pinyin: Dēngshān duì jiǎnchále suǒyǒu zhuāngbèi cái chūfā.
example.english: The mountaineering team checked all their equipment before setting out.
example.fact: Climbers on Mount Everest typically carry supplemental oxygen above 8,000 meters, an altitude nicknamed the 'death zone,' where air pressure is only about a third of sea level — too little oxygen for the human body to ever fully acclimatize, no matter how long it stays.

components.note: 亻 (a person) — 体 concerns the human body or physical form.
本 (root, foundation) — suggests the body as a person's rooted, foundational form. This simplified pairing replaced the traditional character 體, which combined 骨 ('bone') with the phonetic element 豊.
马 (horse) — 验 originally related to examining or testing horses, later extended to 'to test, examine, verify'
佥 (qiān) gives a loose sound connection to 验's reading yàn

example.hanzi: 这次旅行让我体验到了不同的文化。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚxíng ràng wǒ tǐyàn dàole bùtóng de wénhuà.
example.english: This trip let me experience a different culture.
example.fact: Memory researchers describe a 'holiday paradox': new, unfamiliar experiences get encoded with far more detail than routine ones, so a novel trip can feel like it flew by while it's happening but feel much longer than a week at home when you look back on it.

components.note: 木 (tree) — traditionally read as a tree that has borne fruit.
立 (standing) — standing close by to watch it grow, evoking closeness and nurture, extended to 亲's meaning 'close, dear; parent, relative.'
冖 (a roof/house) — the home being welcomed into.
友 (a friend) — brought close into one's home; the traditional form 愛 also includes 心 ('heart') in the middle — the source of 爱's meaning 'to love.'
白 (white, bright) — 的's original meaning was a bright, white spot, as in the white center of an archery target, giving 的 its old meaning 'target, bullseye.'
勺 supplies the character's original sound reading dí, distinct from the common possessive-particle reading de that the character carries today.

example.hanzi: 亲爱的,晚饭已经准备好了。
example.pinyin: Qīn'ài de, wǎnfàn yǐjīng zhǔnbèi hǎo le.
example.english: Darling, dinner is already ready.
example.fact: Relationship research has found that couples who regularly use private pet names and terms of endearment for each other tend to report higher relationship satisfaction, since the small shared ritual reinforces a sense of private, exclusive identity between partners.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 坏 relates to something crumbling or deteriorating, like broken soil.
不 (bù) reflects an old phonetic link that has largely faded in the modern pronunciation huài.
虫 (a small creature) — 蛋 names an egg, historically grouped together with small creatures like insects and reptiles.
延 (yán) is only distantly related in sound to dàn — the connection has drifted apart to the point of being barely recognizable.

example.hanzi: 电影里的坏蛋最后被警察抓住了。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de huàidàn zuìhòu bèi jǐngchá zhuāzhù le.
example.english: The villain in the movie was finally caught by the police.
example.fact: A simple way to test whether an egg is still fresh is to drop it in water: a fresh egg sinks and lies flat, while an old one floats upright or on its side, because the air pocket inside grows larger over time as moisture escapes and air seeps in through the shell's pores.

components.note: A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'

午's oracle-bone form pictured a pestle, a tool for pounding grain. That original meaning was later dropped, and the character was borrowed for its sound to label the seventh of the twelve Earthly Branches — and, by extension, the hour marking midday.

example.hanzi: 我们中午一起去吃饭吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōngwǔ yīqǐ qù chīfàn ba.
example.english: Let's go eat together at noon.
example.fact: 'Solar noon,' the moment the sun reaches its highest point in the sky, rarely matches 12:00 on a clock exactly — it can shift by up to about 16 minutes either way over the course of a year, a discrepancy called the equation of time, caused by Earth's elliptical orbit and axial tilt.

components.note: 录 traditionally depicted a hand-held tool used for carving or writing records — the image behind its meaning 'to record, to write down.'
立 here depicts a tongue positioned to speak.
日 here depicts an open mouth — a tongue forming sound in the mouth gave 音 its meaning 'sound, tone.'

example.hanzi: 他把整个会议都录音了下来。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhěnggè huìyì dōu lùyīnle xiàlái.
example.english: He recorded the entire meeting.
example.fact: The oldest known recording of a human voice that can still be played back today is a 10-second phonautogram made in 1860 by Édouard-Léon Scott de Martinville, seventeen years before Edison's phonograph — it was only successfully played back in 2008 after being scanned and converted to digital audio.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — relates to 照's meaning 'to shine, illuminate; photograph.'
昭 (zhāo) gives a sound hint — 照 is pronounced zhào, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
手 (hand) — depicts a hand raised above the eyes.
目 (eye) — shielding the eyes with a hand to look into the distance gave 看 its meaning 'to look, to see.'

example.hanzi: 奶奶在家照看小孙子。
example.pinyin: Nǎinai zàijiā zhàokàn xiǎo sūnzi.
example.english: Grandma is looking after her little grandson at home.
example.fact: Large-scale surveys on aging have found that roughly two in five grandparents provide regular childcare for their grandchildren, and researchers have linked active grandparenting to measurable benefits for both grandparents' cognitive health and grandchildren's social development.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/place) — reflects 阿's original meaning related to a hill or slope
可 (kě) gives a sound close to 阿's reading ā
门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.

example.hanzi: 牧师祷告结束后,大家一起说:"阿门。"
example.pinyin: Mùshī dǎogào jiéshù hòu, dàjiā yīqǐ shuō: "Āmén."
example.english: After the pastor finished the prayer, everyone said together, "Amen."
example.fact: The word 'amen' comes from Biblical Hebrew, where it means roughly 'so be it' or 'truly.' It has been carried, largely unchanged in pronunciation, across Judaism, Christianity, and Islam for more than two thousand years, making it one of the most widely shared loanwords among unrelated religious traditions.

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — 货 relates to goods that are bought and sold for money
化 (huà) gives a sound distantly related to 货's reading huò, having drifted apart over time
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'

example.hanzi: 一辆货车正在卸货。
example.pinyin: Yī liàng huòchē zhèngzài xièhuò.
example.english: A truck is unloading goods.
example.fact: The U.S. Interstate Highway System, the backbone of modern long-haul trucking, was partly inspired by Germany's autobahn network, which Dwight Eisenhower had seen during World War II. Its construction, beginning in 1956, was the largest public works project in American history at the time.

components.note: 寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'
八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'

example.hanzi: 他在最后一秒钟得分,帮球队赢了比赛。
example.pinyin: Tā zài zuìhòu yī miǎozhōng défēn, bāng qiúduì yíngle bǐsài.
example.english: He scored in the final second, helping the team win the game.
example.fact: In basketball, a shot only counts if the ball leaves the shooter's hand before the game clock reads zero — a rule now enforced with camera systems precise enough to review fractions of a second, adopted across major leagues after several famously disputed buzzer-beater calls in the 1990s.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 编 originally described weaving or knitting threads together.
扁 (biǎn) gives a sound close to biān, with the tone shifted.
车 (cart) — 辑 originally referred to fitting a cart's parts together, extending to 'gather, compile, edit.'
咠 (qì) is distantly related in sound to jí, sharing the same historical initial series (j/q/x) though the two have drifted apart.

example.hanzi: 她是一家杂志的编辑。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yī jiā zázhì de biānjí.
example.english: She is an editor at a magazine.
example.fact: Before word processors, editors marked up manuscripts using a standardized set of proofreading symbols, many still taught today, that trace back to conventions developed by print shops in the 15th and 16th centuries, not long after Gutenberg's press made mass-produced text possible.

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 忘 relates to something slipping from the mind.
亡 (wáng) gives a sound distantly related to wàng, having drifted apart over time.
扌 (hand) — 掉 relates to dropping something from the hand.
卓 (zhuó) reflects an older phonetic connection that has faded in the modern pronunciation diào.

example.hanzi: 她努力想忘掉那段痛苦的记忆。
example.pinyin: Tā nǔlì xiǎng wàngdiào nà duàn tòngkǔ de jìyì.
example.english: She tried hard to forget that painful memory.
example.fact: In the 1880s, psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus tested his own memory and mapped out the 'forgetting curve': without any review, people forget over half of newly learned information within about an hour, and up to 70% within a day — a finding that still underlies modern spaced-repetition study techniques.

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — 性 relates to inner nature or character.
生 (shēng) gives a hint of the sound — 性 is pronounced xìng, a related sound though the initial has shifted.
木 (wood) — 格 originally meant a wooden branch or standard, extended to 'pattern, style, rule.'
各 (gè) gives a sound hint — 格 is pronounced gé, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 她的性格开朗又乐观。
example.pinyin: Tā de xìnggé kāilǎng yòu lèguān.
example.english: Her personality is cheerful and optimistic.
example.fact: Modern psychology's most widely used personality framework, the 'Big Five,' measures traits across just five broad dimensions — openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism — and twin studies suggest genetics accounts for roughly 40 to 60% of the variation in these traits between people.

components.note: 氵 (water) — relates directly to 流's meaning 'to flow.'
㐬 (liú) gives the sound — 流 is also pronounced liú, an exact match.
民 (people) — 氓 (the common people) refers to a nation's subjects.
亡 (wáng) gives a sound distantly related to máng, sharing the same final but having drifted apart in initial consonant over time.

example.hanzi: 警察逮捕了几个街头流氓。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá dàibǔle jǐ gè jiētóu liúmáng.
example.english: Police arrested a few street hoodlums.
example.fact: Criminologists studying urban violence have found it is highly concentrated geographically — in some U.S. cities, over half of all gun violence occurs on less than 5% of city blocks, a pattern that let 'focused deterrence' policing strategies target resources far more precisely than city-wide patrols.

components.note: 犭 (dog) — an old link behind 独's meaning 'alone, single, solitary'
虫 (chóng) gives a loose sound connection to 独's reading dú
無-shaped top pictures a dancer holding decorated sleeves or fans.
舛 below pictures a pair of feet, together giving 舞 its meaning 'to dance.'

example.hanzi: 她在晚会上表演了一段独舞。
example.pinyin: Tā zài wǎnhuì shàng biǎoyǎnle yī duàn dúwǔ.
example.english: She performed a solo dance at the evening party.
example.fact: One of classical ballet's most demanding solo passages, the Black Swan's coda in Swan Lake, requires 32 consecutive fouetté turns performed in place — a feat that pushes a dancer's balance and rotational stamina to its limits.
